content_voiceover: This is a classic boards table pairing cancer predisposition syndromes with their associated CNS tumor types, and it's worth memorizing the highlighted rows. Hereditary retinoblastoma, caused by Rb mutations, predisposes to pineoblastoma, glioma, and meningioma, plus non CNS tumors like osteosarcoma and melanoma. Li Fraumeni syndrome, from TP53 mutations, is associated with multiple brain tumor types, most classically supratentorial PNET, medulloblastoma, and astrocytoma, along with sarcomas, adrenocortical tumors, leukemia, and early breast cancer. Neurofibromatosis type one, NF1 gene, causes optic nerve glioma and astrocytoma, while neurofibromatosis type two, the NF2 gene, causes bilateral acoustic schwannomas, meningiomas, and spinal ependymomas, that bilateral acoustic schwannoma finding is the classic NF2 board buzzword. Beyond the highlighted rows, remember Cowden syndrome with PTEN causing dysplastic cerebellar gangliocytoma, also called Lhermitte Duclos disease, Gorlin syndrome with PTCH causing medulloblastoma and basal cell carcinomas, tuberous sclerosis with TSC1 or TSC2 causing subependymal giant cell astrocytoma, Turcot syndrome with APC or the mismatch repair genes causing medulloblastoma or astrocytoma with colorectal tumors, and von Hippel Lindau with the VHL gene causing hemangioblastoma.
keypoints: Li Fraumeni, TP53, causes multiple brain tumors including medulloblastoma and astrocytoma
NF2 causes bilateral acoustic schwannoma, a classic board buzzword
Tuberous sclerosis causes subependymal giant cell astrocytoma
keypoint_voiceover: The highest yield pairings here are Li Fraumeni and TP53 with multiple brain tumor types including medulloblastoma, neurofibromatosis type two with bilateral acoustic schwannoma, tuberous sclerosis with subependymal giant cell astrocytoma, and von Hippel Lindau with hemangioblastoma. Match the gene to the tumor and you'll cover most exam questions on this topic.
